script.text: Four giant U.S. banks just reported earnings. Most of their shares slipped. Why?
JPMorgan missed Wall Street's forecasts on Tuesday, CNBC reports. Its bond trading revenue fell 4 percent, the first drop in more than two years. Its shares ended the day down 0.9 percent.

Goldman Sachs earned 17.01 dollars a share, against 13.09 expected. Citigroup earned 2.85 against 2.65 expected, on revenue of 23.8 billion dollars. Yet Citigroup shares fell, and Wells Fargo lost 3 percent after its revenue missed.

Reports point to cautious outlooks. Citigroup told analysts to expect trading revenue to fall about 20 percent next quarter. Shares move on expectations, not just results. The S and P 500 closed almost flat.
Will bank trading profits keep growing next quarter? Yes or no?

upload.title: Banks Beat Forecasts, Yet Shares Slip After JPMorgan Miss #shorts
upload.description:
Big U.S. banks reported third-quarter results on Tuesday. CNBC reports JPMorgan missed forecasts, with bond trading revenue down 4% and shares down 0.9%. Goldman Sachs earned $17.01 per share versus $13.09 expected, and Citigroup $2.85 versus $2.65, yet Citigroup shares fell and Wells Fargo lost 3%.

Sources: CNBC, Forbes, Mitrade, Citigroup filing (Oct 13, 2026).
